workingTitle: An interstellar comet carried short-lived icy grains
coreFacts: Zwicky Transient Facility observations followed interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS before and after perihelion.
The inner coma faded faster than the outer coma after perihelion, and the temporarily steep brightness profile coincided with an unusually blue outer coma.
The fading component extended roughly 64,000 to 72,000 kilometres from the comet.
Thermophysical modelling found the observed scale consistent with 5 to 10 micrometre icy grains containing about 0.1 percent absorbing carbonaceous material.
The authors infer that the early post-perihelion coma likely contained a short-lived, volatile-bearing grain population.
caveats: The icy-grain size and composition are model-dependent rather than directly measured.
Dust mass-loss rates depend on assumed grain sizes and residence times.
A fading volatile-bearing component is the authors' preferred interpretation of the linked brightness and colour changes, not a unique direct detection of individual grains.
